notes:
1. Jawaharlal Nehru — Overview

  • Jawaharlal Nehru was one of the foremost leaders of the Indian national movement.
  • He represented:
  • Complete independence.
  • Secular nationalism.
  • Democratic socialism.
  • Scientific temper.
  • Economic planning.
  • Internationalism.
  • He became the first Prime Minister of independent India.
📌 Must-Memorise

Jawaharlal Nehru → Purna Swaraj + Planning + First Prime Minister

2. Birth

  • Jawaharlal Nehru was born on 14 November 1889.
  • He was born at Allahabad in the United Provinces.
📌 Must-Memorise

Nehru → 14 November 1889 → Allahabad

3. Children's Day

  • 14 November is observed in India as Children's Day.
  • Nehru was affectionately associated with children.
📌 Must-Memorise

14 November → Children's Day

4. Popular Name

  • Nehru was popularly called Chacha Nehru.

5. Father

  • His father was Motilal Nehru.
  • Motilal was:
  • A prominent lawyer.
  • Congress leader.
  • Swaraj Party leader.
📌 Must-Memorise

Jawaharlal's Father → Motilal Nehru

6. Mother

  • Jawaharlal Nehru's mother was Swarup Rani Nehru.
📌 Must-Memorise

Mother → Swarup Rani

7. Anand Bhavan

  • The Nehru family's residence at Allahabad became known as Anand Bhavan.
  • It became an important centre of nationalist political activity.
📌 Must-Memorise

Anand Bhavan → Allahabad → Nehru Family

8. Swaraj Bhavan

  • The earlier Nehru family residence was later known as Swaraj Bhavan.
  • It was closely associated with Congress activity.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Allahabad → Anand Bhavan + Swaraj Bhavan

9. Early Education

  • Nehru initially received private education at home.
  • His tutors introduced him to:
  • Science.
  • Literature.
  • History.

10. Theosophical Influence

  • As a young boy, Nehru briefly came into contact with the Theosophical movement.
  • Ferdinand T. Brooks was among his early tutors.

11. Harrow School

  • Nehru went to England and studied at Harrow School.
📌 Must-Memorise

Nehru → Harrow

12. Trinity College, Cambridge

  • Nehru studied at Trinity College, Cambridge.
📌 Must-Memorise

Nehru → Trinity College, Cambridge

13. Natural Sciences

  • At Cambridge, Nehru studied Natural Sciences.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Nehru's Cambridge Subject → Natural Sciences

14. Inner Temple

  • After Cambridge, Nehru studied law at the Inner Temple in London.
📌 Must-Memorise

Nehru → Inner Temple → Law

15. Barrister

  • Nehru was called to the Bar in 1912.
  • He returned to India the same year.

16. Legal Career

  • Nehru initially practised law at the Allahabad High Court.
  • He soon became increasingly interested in nationalist politics.

17. First Congress Session Attended

  • Nehru attended the 1912 Bankipore session of the Indian National Congress.
📌 Must-Memorise

Nehru's Early Congress Participation → Bankipore, 1912

18. Gandhi–Nehru Meeting

  • Nehru met Mahatma Gandhi during the Lucknow Congress session of 1916.
📌 Must-Memorise

Gandhi–Nehru Meeting → Lucknow → 1916

19. Lucknow Congress

The 1916 Lucknow session is also remembered for:

  • Moderate–Extremist reunion.
  • Congress–Muslim League Lucknow Pact.

20. Marriage

  • Jawaharlal Nehru married Kamala Kaul in 1916.
📌 Must-Memorise

Nehru's Wife → Kamala Nehru

21. Kamala Nehru

  • Kamala Nehru participated in:
  • Non-Cooperation.
  • Civil Disobedience.
  • Women's nationalist mobilisation.

22. Indira Gandhi

  • Jawaharlal and Kamala Nehru's daughter was Indira Priyadarshini Gandhi.
  • She later became Prime Minister of India.
📌 Must-Memorise

Jawaharlal Nehru → Father of Indira Gandhi

23. Home Rule Movement

  • Nehru became active during the Home Rule period.
  • The movement was led principally by:
  • Bal Gangadhar Tilak.
  • Annie Besant.

24. Annie Besant

  • Nehru was initially attracted to the Home Rule agitation for greater Indian self-government.

25. Gandhi's Influence

  • Gandhi's emergence transformed Nehru's political career.
  • Nehru increasingly participated in:
  • Mass movements.
  • Peasant struggles.
  • Anti-colonial campaigns.

26. Nehru and Peasant Politics

  • Nehru travelled extensively in the United Provinces.
  • He witnessed:
  • Rural poverty.
  • High rents.
  • Peasant indebtedness.
  • Landlord oppression.

27. Pratapgarh Peasants

  • Peasant movements in districts such as Pratapgarh helped expose Nehru to agrarian grievances.

28. Baba Ramchandra

  • Baba Ramchandra became an important peasant organiser in Awadh.
  • Nehru interacted with the agrarian movement in the region.
📌 Must-Memorise

Baba Ramchandra → Awadh Peasant Movement

29. Non-Cooperation Movement

  • Nehru participated actively in Gandhi's Non-Cooperation Movement from 1920.

30. Imprisonment

  • Nehru was repeatedly arrested during the freedom struggle.
  • Imprisonment became a recurring feature of his political career.

31. Prince of Wales Boycott

  • Nehru participated in agitation associated with the boycott of the Prince of Wales's visit.

32. Allahabad Municipal Board

  • Nehru served as Chairman of the Allahabad Municipal Board during the 1920s.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Nehru → Allahabad Municipal Administration

33. Congress General Secretary

  • Nehru served as General Secretary of the Indian National Congress during important phases of the 1920s.

34. Rise of Younger Leadership

By the late 1920s, two prominent younger Congress leaders were:

  • Jawaharlal Nehru.
  • Subhas Chandra Bose.
📌 Must-Memorise

Young Radical Congress Leadership → Nehru + Bose

35. Complete Independence

  • Nehru favoured complete independence rather than Dominion Status.

36. Anti-Imperialism

  • Nehru saw British rule in India as part of the broader system of imperialism.
  • He connected Indian freedom with anti-imperialist struggles elsewhere.

37. Internationalism

Nehru took strong interest in:

  • European politics.
  • Soviet developments.
  • Asian nationalism.
  • Anti-colonial struggles.

38. Brussels Congress

  • Nehru attended the Congress of Oppressed Nationalities at Brussels in 1927.
📌 Must-Memorise

Nehru → Brussels → 1927

39. League Against Imperialism

  • The Brussels meeting contributed to the formation of the League Against Imperialism.
  • Nehru participated in its international anti-colonial network.

40. Soviet Union Visit

  • Nehru visited the Soviet Union in 1927.
  • He became interested in:
  • Economic planning.
  • Rapid industrialisation.
  • Socialist ideas.
📌 Must-Memorise

Nehru → Soviet Visit → 1927

41. Nehru and Socialism

  • Nehru increasingly believed that political freedom required:
  • Economic equality.
  • Industrial development.
  • Reduction of poverty.

42. Nehru and Marxism

  • Nehru studied Marxist ideas and was influenced by socialist analysis.
  • However, he did not become an orthodox communist.
⚠️ TNPSC Caution

Nehru → Socialist Influence, Not Communist Party Leader

43. Independence for India League

  • Jawaharlal Nehru and Subhas Bose were associated with the Independence for India League.
📌 Must-Memorise

Independence for India League → Nehru + Bose

44. Nehru Report — 1928

  • The Nehru Report was prepared under Motilal Nehru's chairmanship.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Nehru Report → Motilal Nehru

Not Jawaharlal Nehru

45. Dominion Status Debate

  • The Nehru Report favoured Dominion Status.
  • Jawaharlal Nehru and Subhas Bose wanted complete independence.

46. Calcutta Congress — 1928

  • Congress gave the British government a deadline to accept Dominion Status.
  • Otherwise, it would move toward complete independence.

47. Lahore Congress

  • Jawaharlal Nehru was elected president of the Lahore session of the Indian National Congress in December 1929.
📌 Must-Memorise

Lahore Congress → 1929 → Jawaharlal Nehru

48. Importance of Lahore Presidency

  • Nehru's presidency symbolised the rise of a younger, more radical generation in Congress.

49. Purna Swaraj

  • The Lahore Congress adopted Purna Swaraj, or complete independence, as the national objective.
📌 Must-Memorise

Purna Swaraj → Lahore → 1929

50. Ravi River

  • The national flag was hoisted at Lahore on the banks of the Ravi.
📌 Must-Memorise

Lahore Congress → Ravi River

51. Independence Pledge

  • Congress called upon Indians to take a pledge for complete independence.

52. Independence Day — 1930

  • 26 January 1930 was observed throughout India as Independence Day.
📌 Must-Memorise

26 January 1930 → Purna Swaraj Day

53. Why 26 January Matters

  • The historical importance of 26 January 1930 later influenced the choice of 26 January 1950 as the date for the Constitution to come fully into force.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

26 January 1930 → Purna Swaraj

26 January 1950 → Republic

54. Civil Disobedience Movement

  • Nehru participated actively in the Civil Disobedience Movement launched in 1930.

55. Arrest in 1930

  • Nehru was arrested before or during major phases of Civil Disobedience.
  • His imprisonment increased public mobilisation.

56. Salt Movement

  • Although Gandhi led the Dandi March, Nehru strongly supported the wider Civil Disobedience programme.

57. Nehru Family Participation

The freedom struggle involved several members of the Nehru family:

  • Motilal Nehru.
  • Jawaharlal Nehru.
  • Kamala Nehru.
  • Later Indira Gandhi as a young activist.

58. Motilal Nehru's Death

  • Motilal Nehru died in 1931.

59. Gandhi–Irwin Pact

  • Jawaharlal accepted Congress discipline regarding the Gandhi–Irwin Pact despite reservations among younger radicals.

60. Second Round Table Conference

  • Gandhi represented the Congress at the Second Round Table Conference in 1931.
  • Nehru did not represent Congress there.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Second RTC Congress Representative → Gandhi, Not Nehru

61. Renewed Civil Disobedience

  • Nehru was again imprisoned after Civil Disobedience resumed in 1932.

62. Prison as Intellectual Space

  • Nehru used periods of imprisonment to:
  • Read.
  • Write.
  • Study history.
  • Reflect on nationalism and civilisation.

63. Letters from a Father to His Daughter

  • Nehru wrote a series of letters to his daughter Indira explaining natural and human history.
  • They were later published as Letters from a Father to His Daughter.
📌 Must-Memorise

Letters from a Father to His Daughter → Jawaharlal Nehru

64. Glimpses of World History

  • Nehru wrote Glimpses of World History largely as letters from prison to Indira.
📌 Must-Memorise

Glimpses of World History → Nehru

65. Autobiography

  • Nehru wrote An Autobiography while imprisoned.
  • It was published in 1936.
📌 Must-Memorise

An Autobiography → Nehru → 1936

66. Toward Freedom

  • Nehru's autobiography is also known under the title Toward Freedom.

67. The Discovery of India

  • Nehru wrote The Discovery of India while imprisoned at Ahmednagar Fort during the 1940s.
📌 Must-Memorise

The Discovery of India → Ahmednagar Fort

68. Publication

  • The Discovery of India was published in 1946.
📌 Must-Memorise

The Discovery of India → 1946

69. Importance of The Discovery of India

The book examined:

  • Indian civilisation.
  • Cultural unity.
  • Historical continuity.
  • Colonialism.
  • National identity.

70. Ahmednagar Fort

  • Nehru was imprisoned at Ahmednagar Fort following the Quit India Movement.
📌 Must-Memorise

Nehru + Quit India Imprisonment → Ahmednagar Fort

71. Kamala Nehru's Illness

  • Kamala Nehru suffered from tuberculosis.
  • She underwent treatment in Europe.

72. Kamala Nehru's Death

  • Kamala Nehru died in 1936 in Switzerland.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kamala Nehru → Died 1936

73. Nehru and Secularism

  • Nehru regarded secularism as essential to India's unity.
  • He opposed political mobilisation based on religious majoritarianism.

74. Nehru's Nationalism

His nationalism emphasised:

  • Civic equality.
  • Religious pluralism.
  • Political democracy.
  • Cultural diversity.

75. Nehru and Science

  • Nehru strongly valued:
  • Scientific inquiry.
  • Rational thinking.
  • Modern technological development.

76. Scientific Temper

  • Scientific temper became one of the ideas most closely associated with Nehru's vision of modern India.
📌 Must-Memorise

Scientific Temper → Jawaharlal Nehru

77. Nehru and Industrialisation

  • Nehru believed that large-scale industrialisation was essential to:
  • Reduce poverty.
  • Modernise agriculture.
  • Build national strength.

78. Nehru and Gandhi — Economic Difference

Gandhi emphasised:

  • Village economy.
  • Decentralisation.
  • Small-scale industries.

Nehru placed greater emphasis on:

  • Heavy industry.
  • Modern science.
  • Central economic planning.
⚠️ TNPSC Favourite Comparison

Gandhi → Village-Centred

Nehru → Industrial-Planning Orientation

79. Shared Political Relationship

  • Despite ideological differences, Gandhi and Nehru maintained a close political relationship.
  • Gandhi increasingly saw Nehru as an important leader of the next generation.

80. Lucknow Congress — 1936

  • Jawaharlal Nehru presided over the Lucknow Congress session in 1936.
📌 Must-Memorise

Lucknow Congress → 1936 → Jawaharlal Nehru

81. Socialist Emphasis at Lucknow

  • Nehru's presidential address reflected his growing commitment to socialism and anti-imperialism.

82. Faizpur Congress — 1936/37

  • Nehru presided over the Faizpur session, held in December 1936 and commonly associated with the 1937 Congress cycle.
📌 Must-Memorise

Faizpur → First Rural Congress Session → Nehru

83. First Rural Congress Session

  • Faizpur was the first Congress session held in a rural setting.
📌 Must-Memorise

First Rural INC Session → Faizpur

84. Agrarian Focus

  • Faizpur placed greater emphasis on:
  • Peasant conditions.
  • Agriculture.
  • Rural poverty.

85. Congress Socialist Pressure

  • During the 1930s, Nehru maintained close intellectual sympathy with socialist groups, though he did not join the Congress Socialist Party as a formal factional leader.

86. National Planning Committee

  • The Congress established the National Planning Committee in 1938 during Subhas Chandra Bose's presidency.
📌 Must-Memorise

National Planning Committee → 1938

87. Chairman

  • Jawaharlal Nehru was appointed Chairman.
📌 Must-Memorise

National Planning Committee Chairman → Nehru

88. Planning Committee Objectives

It examined:

  • Industrialisation.
  • Agriculture.
  • National resources.
  • Employment.
  • Economic development.

89. Bose–Nehru Planning Link

⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Bose Presidency → Committee Established

Nehru → Committee Chairman

90. Haripura Session

  • Subhas Bose presided at Haripura in 1938.
  • Nehru remained a major Congress figure despite differences with Bose and Gandhi-aligned leaders.

91. Tripuri Crisis

  • In 1939, Bose's re-election created a major internal Congress crisis.
  • Nehru attempted to navigate between ideological sympathy with Bose's radicalism and his wider commitment to Congress unity.

92. Second World War

  • Britain declared India at war with Germany in September 1939 without consulting Indian political representatives.

93. Nehru and Fascism

  • Nehru strongly opposed:
  • Fascism.
  • Nazism.
  • Imperialism.
  • He nevertheless rejected India's involuntary participation in Britain's war without freedom.

94. Congress Ministries Resign

  • Congress provincial ministries resigned in 1939.

95. August Offer

  • Nehru and Congress found the August Offer of 1940 inadequate.

96. Individual Satyagraha

  • Gandhi launched Individual Satyagraha in 1940.

97. First Individual Satyagrahi

  • Vinoba Bhave was the first Individual Satyagrahi.

98. Nehru as Second Satyagrahi

  • Jawaharlal Nehru was chosen as the second prominent Individual Satyagrahi.
📌 Must-Memorise

Second Individual Satyagrahi → Jawaharlal Nehru

99. Arrest

  • Nehru was arrested for his Individual Satyagraha activities.

100. Cripps Mission

  • Nehru participated in Congress deliberations over the Cripps proposals of 1942.

101. Cripps Proposals Rejected

  • Congress rejected the proposals because they did not provide immediate effective transfer of power.

102. Quit India Movement

  • Nehru participated in the Congress decision to launch Quit India in August 1942.
📌 Must-Memorise

Nehru → Quit India Leadership → 1942

103. Arrest on 9 August

  • Nehru and other senior Congress leaders were arrested on 9 August 1942.

104. Ahmednagar Fort Detention

  • Nehru was confined for a long period at Ahmednagar Fort.

105. Duration of Imprisonment

  • The Quit India imprisonment became one of Nehru's longest periods of detention.

106. Discovery of India in Prison

  • It was during this incarceration that he wrote The Discovery of India.

107. Release

  • Nehru and other senior Congress leaders were released in 1945 as the political situation changed after World War II.

108. INA Trials

  • Nehru participated in the defence campaign for Indian National Army officers in 1945–46.
📌 Must-Memorise

Nehru → INA Defence

109. Legal Robes

  • Nehru appeared in barrister's robes during the INA defence proceedings.

110. INA Trial Defendants

The famous first trial involved:

  • Shah Nawaz Khan.
  • Prem Kumar Sahgal.
  • Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon.

111. Nehru and Bose

  • Nehru and Bose had shared several anti-imperialist and socialist concerns.
  • They differed later over:
  • Wartime alliances.
  • Political strategy.
⚠️ TNPSC Caution

Nehru and Bose → Shared Radical Nationalism Early, Different Wartime Paths Later

112. Cabinet Mission

  • The British Cabinet Mission arrived in India in 1946.
  • Nehru participated in negotiations over constitutional transfer of power.
📌 Must-Memorise

Cabinet Mission → 1946

113. Congress Presidency — 1946 Question

  • Maulana Abul Kalam Azad had served as Congress president during much of the wartime period.
  • J.B. Kripalani became Congress president later in 1946.
  • Nehru became the dominant Congress leader in negotiations and government formation.

114. Interim Government

  • The Interim Government was formed on 2 September 1946.
📌 Must-Memorise

Interim Government → 2 September 1946

115. Nehru's Position

  • Nehru became Vice-President of the Viceroy's Executive Council.
  • In practice, he functioned as the head of the Interim Government.
📌 Must-Memorise

Interim Government Effective Head → Jawaharlal Nehru

116. External Affairs

  • Nehru handled External Affairs and Commonwealth Relations in the Interim Government.

117. Muslim League Entry

  • The Muslim League initially stayed out of the Interim Government but later joined it.

118. Partition Crisis

  • Congress–League conflict, communal violence and constitutional deadlock ultimately led to acceptance of Partition.

119. Nehru and Partition

  • Nehru had long opposed communal division.
  • By 1947, Congress leaders accepted Partition as part of the transfer-of-power settlement.
⚠️ TNPSC Caution

Acceptance of Partition → Political Compromise in 1947, Not Nehru's Original Goal

120. Mountbatten Plan

  • The 3 June 1947 Plan provided the framework for Partition and transfer of power.
📌 Must-Memorise

3 June Plan → 1947 → Partition Framework

121. Indian Independence Act

  • The British Parliament passed the Indian Independence Act in July 1947.
📌 Must-Memorise

Indian Independence Act → 1947

122. Independence

  • India became independent on 15 August 1947.

123. First Prime Minister

  • Jawaharlal Nehru became India's first Prime Minister.
📌 Must-Memorise

First Prime Minister of India → Jawaharlal Nehru

124. Prime Ministerial Tenure

  • Nehru served continuously as Prime Minister from:
  • 15 August 1947.
  • Until his death on 27 May 1964.
📌 Must-Memorise

Nehru PM → 1947–1964

125. "Tryst with Destiny"

  • Nehru delivered his famous "Tryst with Destiny" speech on the eve of independence.
📌 Must-Memorise

Tryst with Destiny → Jawaharlal Nehru

126. Date of Speech

  • It was delivered late on 14 August 1947 as India approached independence at midnight.

127. Constituent Assembly Setting

  • Nehru delivered the speech before the Constituent Assembly.

128. Objectives Resolution

  • Nehru introduced the Objectives Resolution in the Constituent Assembly on 13 December 1946.
📌 Must-Memorise

Objectives Resolution → Jawaharlal Nehru → 13 December 1946

129. Adoption of Objectives Resolution

  • The Constituent Assembly adopted it on 22 January 1947.
📌 Must-Memorise

Objectives Resolution Adopted → 22 January 1947

130. Importance of Objectives Resolution

It laid down ideas relating to:

  • Sovereignty.
  • Democracy.
  • Justice.
  • Equality.
  • Federalism.
  • Rights.

131. Preamble Link

  • The Objectives Resolution strongly influenced the Preamble of the Constitution.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Objectives Resolution → Foundation for Preamble

132. Nehru and Constitution-Making

  • Nehru was not Chairman of the Drafting Committee.
  • B.R. Ambedkar held that position.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Objectives Resolution → Nehru

Drafting Committee → Ambedkar

133. Union Powers Committee

  • Nehru chaired important Constituent Assembly committees, including the Union Powers Committee.
📌 Must-Memorise

Union Powers Committee → Jawaharlal Nehru

134. Union Constitution Committee

  • Nehru also chaired the Union Constitution Committee.
📌 Must-Memorise

Union Constitution Committee → Nehru

135. States Committee

  • Nehru played an important role in constitutional relations involving princely states and the Union.

136. Post-Independence Challenges

His government faced:

  • Partition violence.
  • Refugee rehabilitation.
  • Princely-state integration.
  • Kashmir conflict.
  • Economic reconstruction.
  • Food shortages.

137. Princely States — Main Leaders

  • Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and V.P. Menon handled much of the detailed integration of princely states.
  • Nehru participated at the highest political level.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Primary Administrative Integration of Princely States → Patel + V.P. Menon

138. Nehru and Democracy

  • Nehru strongly supported:
  • Parliamentary government.
  • Regular elections.
  • Civil institutions.
  • Opposition politics.

139. First General Election

  • India's first general elections were held in 1951–52.
📌 Must-Memorise

First General Elections → 1951–52

140. Universal Adult Franchise

  • Independent India adopted universal adult franchise from its first general election.
📌 Must-Memorise

India → Universal Adult Franchise from Beginning of Republic

141. Election Commission

  • The Election Commission organised India's first enormous democratic electoral exercise.

142. Nehru and Secular State

  • Nehru strongly defended a state that did not privilege one religion over others.

143. Religious Freedom

  • His political outlook emphasised:
  • Citizenship.
  • Equal rights.
  • Religious pluralism.

144. Democratic Socialism

  • Nehru's economic approach is commonly described as democratic socialism.
📌 Must-Memorise

Nehru → Democratic Socialism

145. Mixed Economy

  • Independent India adopted a mixed economy combining:
  • Public sector.
  • Private enterprise.
📌 Must-Memorise

Nehru Era → Mixed Economy

146. Planning Commission

  • The Planning Commission was established in 1950.
📌 Must-Memorise

Planning Commission → 1950

147. Chairman of Planning Commission

  • The Prime Minister served as Chairman of the Planning Commission.
  • Nehru therefore became its first Chairman.
📌 Must-Memorise

First Planning Commission Chairman → Nehru

148. Five-Year Plans

  • Planned economic development was implemented through Five-Year Plans.

149. First Five-Year Plan

  • The First Five-Year Plan covered 1951–1956.
📌 Must-Memorise

First Five-Year Plan → 1951–56

150. First Plan Priority

  • It placed major emphasis on:
  • Agriculture.
  • Irrigation.
  • Rehabilitation.

151. Second Five-Year Plan

  • The Second Five-Year Plan covered 1956–1961.
📌 Must-Memorise

Second Five-Year Plan → 1956–61

152. Mahalanobis Model

  • The Second Plan is strongly associated with statistician P.C. Mahalanobis.
📌 Must-Memorise

Second Plan → P.C. Mahalanobis

153. Heavy Industry

  • The Second Plan emphasised:
  • Heavy industry.
  • Capital goods.
  • Public-sector development.

154. Public Sector

  • Nehru viewed strategic public-sector industries as essential for rapid national development.

155. Industrial Policy Resolution 1956

  • The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 strengthened the role of the public sector in key industries.
📌 Must-Memorise

Industrial Policy Resolution → 1956

156. Dams

  • Nehru strongly supported multipurpose river-valley projects.

157. "Temples of Modern India"

  • Large dams and development projects were often described by Nehru as symbols or "temples" of modern India's development.
📌 Must-Memorise

Temples of Modern India → Major Development Projects / Dams

158. Bhakra-Nangal

  • Bhakra-Nangal became one of the most famous large multipurpose projects associated with the Nehru era.

159. Hirakud

  • Hirakud Dam in Odisha was another major multipurpose project developed during this period.

160. Damodar Valley

  • Damodar Valley Corporation drew inspiration partly from multipurpose river-development models.

161. Scientific Institutions

Nehru strongly supported institutions for:

  • Science.
  • Engineering.
  • Atomic research.
  • Higher education.

162. Indian Institutes of Technology

  • IITs expanded during the Nehru era.
  • IIT Kharagpur was the first IIT.
📌 Must-Memorise

First IIT → Kharagpur

163. IIT Kharagpur

  • IIT Kharagpur was established in 1951.
📌 Must-Memorise

IIT Kharagpur → 1951

164. AIIMS

  • All India Institute of Medical Sciences was established in New Delhi in 1956.
📌 Must-Memorise

AIIMS → 1956

165. Atomic Energy

  • India's atomic-energy programme developed under Homi J. Bhabha with strong political backing from Nehru.
📌 Must-Memorise

Homi J. Bhabha → Indian Atomic Energy Programme

166. Atomic Energy Commission

  • The Atomic Energy Commission was established in 1948.
📌 Must-Memorise

Atomic Energy Commission → 1948

167. CSIR and Research

  • The post-independence government expanded scientific laboratories and research institutions, building on earlier institutional foundations.

168. Scientific Policy Resolution

  • India's Scientific Policy Resolution was adopted in 1958.
📌 Must-Memorise

Scientific Policy Resolution → 1958

169. Nehru and Scientific Temper

  • Nehru regarded scientific thinking as necessary not only for laboratories but for public life and social development.

170. Education

  • His government supported expansion of:
  • Universities.
  • Technical institutes.
  • Scientific education.

171. University Grants Commission

  • The University Grants Commission was formally established by law in 1956 after earlier organisational development.
📌 Must-Memorise

UGC Act → 1956

172. Foreign Policy

Nehru's foreign policy emphasised:

  • Anti-colonialism.
  • Peaceful coexistence.
  • Non-alignment.
  • Asian-African solidarity.

173. Non-Alignment

  • India did not formally join either the US-led or Soviet-led military bloc during the Cold War.
📌 Must-Memorise

Nehru → Non-Alignment

174. Meaning of Non-Alignment

  • Non-alignment did not mean political neutrality on every international issue.
  • It meant maintaining independent judgement and freedom of foreign-policy choice.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Non-Alignment ≠ Permanent Neutrality

175. Panchsheel

  • India and China articulated the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence in 1954.
📌 Must-Memorise

Panchsheel → 1954
